report: Tim Austin: Some Recent Developments in Structural Ergodic Theory
conclusion: No actionable mathematical mistake found in the 45 inspected files (3001-300Z and 3010-3019). The requested high-risk topics are covered. This is not build/navigation acceptance or approval of later changes.

sources.actually_read: All mathematical body text: section 1, sections 2.1-2.3, sections 3.1-3.11. Selected references only; not the entire bibliography.
sources.limitation: The survey suppresses some background hypotheses. Supporting original theorem statements below were consulted rather than copying the compressed formulations verbatim.

sources.actually_read: Introduction pp. 1-6 through the theorem discussion/update, especially the Rokhlin definitions, Theorem 1.1 and Corollaries 1.2-1.3. Did not audit the deep proof.
sources.focus: Nonatomic ergodic actions, not necessarily free; strict prescribed-distribution generator threshold; countable generating partitions; free amenable Rokhlin/KS equality.

sources.actually_read: Abstract; introduction Theorem 1.1, Corollaries 1.2-1.4 and surrounding discussion (PDF pp. 4-5). Did not audit the proof.
sources.focus: Free ergodic action of a countably infinite group; H(base) <= Rokhlin entropy; nonamenable positive-entropy corollary.

sources.actually_read: Abstract and section 1, especially Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2. Did not audit the isomorphism construction.
sources.focus: Countably infinite groups for equal-entropy isomorphism; sofic groups for the converse.

sources.actually_read: Abstract and Theorem 1 on PDF p. 2, including the following cyclic-action discussion. Did not audit the random-labeling proof.
sources.focus: Every free action of a countably infinite group weakly contains the Bernoulli actions; ergodicity is not required.

sources.actually_read: Sections 1.1-1.4, especially Theorems A-C, Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3 with its quantifier-order remark; section 2.1 and section 2.2 through the microstate-existence definition. Did not audit the shattering proof.
sources.focus: Direct Bernoulli factors versus ordinary factors; k-uniform permutation ensemble with k dividing n; high-probability good sets chosen before all factors.

sources.actually_read: Introduction definition of completely positive entropy and Corollary 1.2 (PDF p. 3); Definition 4.6 and Corollary 4.7 with its proof (PDF pp. 24-25). Did not audit the underlying entropy theorem.
sources.focus: Ordinary completely positive sofic entropy suffices for the stated embedding of the reduced Koopman representation; do not incorrectly demand outer CPE for this particular corollary.

sources.actually_read: Definitions 5.5 and 5.9; section 7.1 trace-convergence hypothesis and its free-group specialization; Theorem 7.2 statement; Lemma 7.3 statement and proof; Proposition 12.8(a) statement. Did not audit the underlying determinantal or random-matrix proofs.
sources.focus: Scalar volume normalization, expectation/log order, zeroth-order speed and mollification formula under superexponential trace convergence.

verified_checks.checked: Countably infinite group and nontrivial finite base are explicit where needed. Independently checked the disjoint-coordinate-pair proof of essential freeness.

Countable generating partitions; ergodic scope; free amenable Rokhlin/KS equality; nonatomicity and strict H(p) threshold for a prescribed generator; equality endpoint restricted to the classical Z case. Recomputed the two-cycle counterexample and block-entropy equality argument.
Free ergodic Sinai theorem includes the non-strict entropy endpoint; nonamenable amplification starts from a nontrivial Bernoulli input; factors are distinguished from product splittings.

Recomputed left-shift equivariance and the right-multiplication Ornstein-Weiss formula Phi(x)_g=(x_g+x_ga,x_g+x_gb). The finite-forest rank count gives independent fair edge bits and uniform four-symbol output.
verified_checks.method: Independent coordinate and finite-forest calculation, not a claim to have read the original Ornstein-Weiss proof.

verified_checks.checked: Weak-containment direction, nonatomic tower hypothesis, tower boundary bound and finite-window transfer of model existence are consistent. No model-count monotonicity is asserted.

Checked exact versus approximate homomorphisms, normalization, finite-window injectivity, empirical multiplicities, ambient probability neighborhoods, a common subsequence, infimum/limsup order and log(0)=-infinity.
Independently checked the O(|F|^2/N) variance bound, typical-label probability lower bound, multinomial upper bound, product-count inequality and finite-base avoidance of infinity-minus-infinity.

Uniform independent permutations for a fixed finite free generating set yield fixed-word asymptotic freeness in probability by the first-moment argument. That argument alone is not an almost-sure whole-sequence assertion.

h^0 uses log P(model space nonempty), not expected log count. mu weakly contained in nu implies h^0(mu)>=h^0(nu). The high-probability consequence of h^0=0 is along a common subsequence; removing it is Question 3.15(a).

Annealed entropy places expectation before logarithm. The quenched definition uses log-plus and the h^0=0 condition, otherwise -infinity. Corollary 3.20 changes limsup to liminf after shrinking neighborhoods; it does not give a limit at each fixed neighborhood.

For k>r>=3 the LDPC example has no nontrivial DIRECT Bernoulli factor, not no ordinary Bernoulli factor. The ensemble is uniform on homomorphisms whose generators consist of k-cycles, with k dividing n. The high-probability good sets precede quantification over all factors.

Weak Pinsker residual entropy is strictly small, not zero; only direct Bernoulli factors enter h^WP. Countably infinite free amenable scope and finite-entropy arithmetic restrictions are explicit. Quoted general versions are distinguished from the finite-generator calculations.
Recomputed the 1/(2n) edge-count normalization with loops and parallel edges. The random-graph convergence conclusion remains conditional on Question 3.15(a).

Verified the elementary integer-variable bounds h^0<=h^ann<=h^0+log|A|. The rare-event example is explicitly abstract, not an asserted realizable system. Product weak-containment gives the stated minimum upper bound, not unproved additivity.
verified_checks.method: Independent elementary probability and factor-map calculation.

verified_checks.checked: Second-variable-linear inner product and positive-definite matrix identity agree. Recomputed the scalar AP scaling law using real dimension 2d. Uniform Haar free-group representations satisfy the trace hypothesis for the stated mollification formula.
The independent-block proof handles nonergodic stationary measures: checked block-mean expectation, 1/m variance bound, cyclic boundary proportion and finite-pattern union bound.
verified_checks.method: Independent verification of the writer's block-sampling proof.

verified_checks.checked: Checked ordinary CPE versus outer CPE directly in Hayes. The reduced Koopman representation embeds into a countable amplification of the left regular representation; the page does not claim this alone gives Bernoulli isomorphism.
